title: Bass and Treble Amplifier Controls
description: Interactive simulation of classic amplifier frequency response with adjustable bass and treble controls.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Signal Processing
Audio
Equalization
Frequency Response
learningObjectives: Predict how raising the bass slider above 50 lifts the frequency response curve above 0 dB below the 500 Hz low-shelf cutoff while leaving treble frequencies unchanged
Explain why the frequency axis uses a logarithmic scale, given that human pitch perception is ratio-based and the audible range spans 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz
Interpret gain in decibels on the -15 dB to +15 dB axis, recognizing that +6 dB roughly doubles perceived loudness and 0 dB is unity gain
Distinguish the low-shelf filter acting below 500 Hz from the high-shelf filter acting above 2,000 Hz by the shape of the response curve
Design slider settings that produce a flat response, a bass-boosted response, and a treble-cut response
